kurs:u02.untertitel: Art. 31 UPCA with the Brussels Ia Regulation, Art. 33 UPCA with “the same parties” and the three options for the counterclaim, the Preliminary objection under R. 19 to 21 RoP and R. 333 RoP
kurs:u02.beschreibung: Four stages of examining jurisdiction before the UPC: international jurisdiction under the Brussels Ia Regulation (Sinocare/Abbott, Dyson/Dreame, NUC/Hurom), subject-matter jurisdiction under Art. 32 UPCA, the correct division under Art. 33 UPCA (Barco/Yealink, Meril/Edwards, Seoul Viosys/Emporia, Pari/Philips) and the objection by way of the Preliminary objection (Roku/Dolby, Vivo/Sun Patent, Sun Patent/Vivo, Netgear/Huawei).

einheit:u02a-0.titel: Examination scheme: jurisdiction of the UPC
einheit:u02a-0.text: From the applicability of the UPCA through international and subject-matter jurisdiction to the choice of division and the defendant's Preliminary objection – this is the order in which the exam tests it, and the order in which R. 13.1(i) RoP requires the information in the Statement of claim.

einheit:u02a-1.text: **First**, the applicability of the UPCA: Unitary Patent or bundle patent without an opt-out (Art. 3, 83 UPCA). **Second**, international jurisdiction: Art. 31 UPCA refers to the **Brussels Ia Regulation**, which treats the UPC as a common court in Art. 71a to 71d Brussels Ia Regulation. The UPC has jurisdiction over defendants domiciled in a Member State (Art. 4 Brussels Ia Regulation) and – irrespective of domicile – over infringements in the territory of the Contracting Member States (Art. 7(2) Brussels Ia Regulation in conjunction with Art. 71b(2) Brussels Ia Regulation): the place where the damage occurs is where infringing products are intended for the market and are acquired via third parties, even if the defendant acts in a third country (Sinocare/Abbott; Dyson/Dreame). A defendant who enters an appearance without contesting jurisdiction establishes it (Art. 26 Brussels Ia Regulation) – but only with its first written pleading, not by accessing the CMS (NUC/Hurom). **Third**, subject-matter jurisdiction: Art. 32(1) UPCA contains an exhaustive list (infringement, declarations of non-infringement, provisional measures, revocation, counterclaims, provisional protection, prior use, compensation for licences, EPO decisions); everything else – entitlement claims, employee inventions, licence agreements – remains with the national courts (Art. 32(2) UPCA). **Fourth**, the division: infringement actions go to the local or regional division at the **place of infringement** or the **defendant's domicile** (Art. 33(1) UPCA), revocation actions and actions for declarations to the **central division** (Art. 33(4) UPCA). The first table sorts the types of action; the second shows how the defendant contests jurisdiction: with the **Preliminary objection** (R. 19 RoP) within one month, not only in the Statement of defence (R. 23 RoP).

gruppe:u02a-2.titel: Made in Shenzhen, sold in Europe
gruppe:u02a-2.sachverhalt: A-Ltd. from Hong Kong manufactures blood glucose sensors in China and sells them to an intermediary in Singapore. Via distribution companies, they reach German pharmacies bearing a CE marking and with German instructions for use. Patent proprietor B sues A-Ltd. before a German local division.

einheit:u02a-2a.titel: Reference to the Brussels Ia Regulation
einheit:u02a-2a.frage: Which rules govern the international jurisdiction of the UPC?
optionen: The code of civil procedure of the state in which the division sits
loesung: The second answer is correct. Art. 31 UPCA refers to the **Brussels Ia Regulation**. Art. 71a to 71d Brussels Ia Regulation treat the UPC as a **common court** of several Member States, which can have jurisdiction like a court of a Member State.
einheit:u02a-2a.abschnitt: Art. 31 UPCA, Art. 71b Brussels Ia Regulation: place where the damage occurs

einheit:u02a-2b.frage: Can A-Ltd. be sued before the UPC, even though it is not domiciled in a Member State?
loesung: **Yes!** The UPC has jurisdiction over defendants not domiciled in a Member State if the **place where the damage occurs** is in the territory of the Contracting Member States (Art. 71b(2) Brussels Ia Regulation in conjunction with Art. 7(2) Brussels Ia Regulation). Domicile is then irrelevant.
einheit:u02a-2b.abschnitt: Art. 31 UPCA, Art. 71b Brussels Ia Regulation: place where the damage occurs

einheit:u02a-2c.frage: Is the place where the damage occurs in Germany, even though A-Ltd. itself only acts in Asia?
loesung: **Yes!** If products are **manufactured and sold for the Contracting Member States**, damage threatens there through their acquisition via third parties, even if the defendant itself acts outside the territory (Sinocare/Abbott). The CE marking and the German instructions for use show which market the products are intended for.
einheit:u02a-2c.merke: Whoever produces for the European market infringes there: the place of damage brings the third-country defendant before the UPC.
einheit:u02a-2c.abschnitt: Art. 31 UPCA, Art. 71b Brussels Ia Regulation: place where the damage occurs

einheit:u02a-2d.frage: Can B sue two European distribution companies of the A group together with A-Ltd.?
loesung: **Yes!** Several defendants of the same group that distribute the same embodiments may be sued together under Art. 8(1) Brussels Ia Regulation. As a common court, the UPC has jurisdiction over all infringements in a Contracting Member State irrespective of domicile (LD Hamburg, Dyson/Dreame).
einheit:u02a-2d.abwandlung: B also wants to sue two distribution companies of the A group in Germany and France that distribute the same sensors.
einheit:u02a-2d.abschnitt: Art. 31 UPCA, Art. 71b Brussels Ia Regulation: place where the damage occurs

einheit:u02a-2e.titel: Choice of division against third-country defendants
einheit:u02a-2e.frage: Is B limited to the local division of the place of infringement in its action against A-Ltd.?
loesung: **No!** The **choice of division** must be distinguished from international jurisdiction. Against defendants not domiciled in a Contracting Member State, an action may be brought at the place of infringement **or before the central division** (Art. 33(1) UPCA, third subparagraph).
einheit:u02a-2e.abschnitt: Art. 31 UPCA, Art. 71b Brussels Ia Regulation: place where the damage occurs

gruppe:u02a-3.sachverhalt: The Korean company H-Co. is sued before a local division. Its representative retrieves the file in the electronic case management system (CMS) using the access code served. Three weeks later, H-Co. lodges a Preliminary objection contesting international jurisdiction.

einheit:u02a-3a.frage: Can H-Co. itself establish the UPC's jurisdiction by entering an appearance without objection?
loesung: **Yes!** Under Art. 26(1) Brussels Ia Regulation, a court acquires jurisdiction where the defendant enters an appearance **without contesting jurisdiction**. This also applies to the UPC (Art. 31 UPCA).
einheit:u02a-3a.abschnitt: Art. 26 Brussels Ia Regulation: appearance without objection

einheit:u02a-3b.titel: A download is not an appearance
einheit:u02a-3b.frage: Does retrieving the file in the CMS already amount to entering an appearance?
loesung: **No!** In electronic proceedings (Art. 44 UPCA, R. 4.1 RoP), access with the access code is merely the **technical first step** towards learning of the action at all. It involves no deliberate decision in favour of jurisdiction (NUC/Hurom).
einheit:u02a-3b.merke: Entering an appearance is a procedural declaration, not a download.
einheit:u02a-3b.abschnitt: Art. 26 Brussels Ia Regulation: appearance without objection

einheit:u02a-3c.frage: With what does the defendant first enter an appearance before the UPC?
optionen: With retrieving the file in the CMS
With the first written pleading: Preliminary objection or Statement of defence
loesung: The third answer is correct. Only with the **first written pleading**, the Preliminary objection under R. 19 RoP or the Statement of defence under R. 23 RoP, does the defendant decide for or against jurisdiction (NUC/Hurom).
einheit:u02a-3c.abschnitt: Art. 26 Brussels Ia Regulation: appearance without objection

loesung: **Yes!** The Preliminary objection must be lodged **within one month** of service of the Statement of claim (R. 19.1 RoP). Three weeks is within the time limit.
einheit:u02a-3d.abschnitt: Art. 26 Brussels Ia Regulation: appearance without objection

einheit:u02a-3e.frage: Can H-Co. still contest jurisdiction on appeal?
loesung: **No!** Without a timely Preliminary objection, jurisdiction is deemed **accepted** (R. 19.7 RoP). The objection is then also lost on appeal (Sinocare/Abbott).
einheit:u02a-3e.abwandlung: H-Co. does not lodge a Preliminary objection, defends itself on the merits and contests jurisdiction only on appeal.
einheit:u02a-3e.abschnitt: Art. 26 Brussels Ia Regulation: appearance without objection

einheit:u02c-0.text: **Art. 33 UPCA** allocates actions to the divisions. Infringement actions go to the local or regional division of the **place of infringement** (Art. 33(1)(a) UPCA) or of the **defendant's domicile** (Art. 33(1)(b) UPCA); against defendants not domiciled in a Contracting Member State, also to the central division (Art. 33(1) UPCA, third subparagraph). A pending infringement action bars further infringement actions between the same parties on the same patent before other divisions (Art. 33(2) UPCA). If the defendant files a **counterclaim for revocation**, the local division has three options (Art. 33(3) UPCA). Revocation actions and actions for declarations of non-infringement belong to the **central division**, unless an infringement action between the same parties is already pending (Art. 33(4) UPCA). An opposition at the EPO is not a prerequisite for a revocation action (Art. 33(8) UPCA).

gruppe:u02a-4.titel: The website can be accessed everywhere
gruppe:u02a-4.sachverhalt: B-NV applies to the Hamburg Local Division for provisional measures against the Chinese company Y-Ltd. and its distribution partner V-GmbH, which has its seat in Munich. Y-Ltd. offers the contested conference systems via a German-language website accessible in Germany.

einheit:u02a-4a.frage: Can B-NV choose freely between the place of infringement (Art. 33(1)(a) UPCA) and the defendant's domicile (Art. 33(1)(b) UPCA)?
loesung: **Yes!** Art. 33(1) UPCA gives the claimant the **choice** between the division of the state of infringement (point (a)) and that of the defendant's domicile (point (b)). There is no order of priority (Barco/Yealink).
einheit:u02a-4a.abschnitt: Art. 33(1) UPCA: place of infringement or defendant's domicile

einheit:u02a-4b.frage: Must the infringement have been committed specifically in the district of the Hamburg Local Division?
loesung: **No!** For Art. 33(1)(a) UPCA, what matters is the **Contracting Member State** in which the infringement has occurred or may occur, not the division's district within Germany.
einheit:u02a-4b.abschnitt: Art. 33(1) UPCA: place of infringement or defendant's domicile

einheit:u02a-4c.frage: Is an offer via a website accessible in Germany sufficient as an infringement in the territory?
loesung: **Yes!** It suffices to establish acts of infringement in the territory, such as an **offer via a website accessible there**. The examination of competence is summary; there is no full taking of evidence (Barco/Yealink).
einheit:u02a-4c.merke: Place of infringement or domicile – the claimant chooses; an accessible website suffices.
einheit:u02a-4c.abschnitt: Art. 33(1) UPCA: place of infringement or defendant's domicile

einheit:u02a-4d.frage: If the chosen division lacks competence, is the case referred to a competent division?
loesung: **Yes!** The competence of the division is an internal matter of the UPC. If the division lacks competence, the case is **referred** once the claimant indicates a competent division (R. 19.5 RoP), for reasons of efficiency also in summary proceedings (Barco/Yealink).
einheit:u02a-4d.abwandlung: B-NV could not have shown any infringement in Germany.
einheit:u02a-4d.abschnitt: Art. 33(1) UPCA: place of infringement or defendant's domicile

einheit:u02a-4e.frage: Can B-NV sue several defendants at the domicile of one of them if they have no business dealings with each other?
loesung: **No!** An action against several defendants requires a **commercial relationship** between them and **the same alleged infringement** (Art. 33(1)(b) UPCA, second sentence).
einheit:u02a-4e.abschnitt: Art. 33(1) UPCA: place of infringement or defendant's domicile

gruppe:u02a-5.sachverhalt: Patent proprietor E sues the Indian company M-Ltd. and its German subsidiary before a local division. Afterwards, the Italian sister company M-Srl brings a revocation action against the same patent before the central division. E considers the central division to lack competence under Art. 33(4) UPCA.

einheit:u02a-5a.frage: Are M-Srl and the defendants “the same parties” because they belong to the same group?
loesung: **No!** Art. 33(4) UPCA only bars the central division if an infringement action on the same patent is already pending between **the same parties**. This in principle requires **identity of the legal entities**; belonging to the same group is not sufficient (Meril/Edwards).
einheit:u02a-5a.abschnitt: Art. 33(2) and 33(4) UPCA: the same parties

einheit:u02a-5b.frage: When are two legal entities exceptionally deemed to be the same party?
optionen: If a judgment against one would have res judicata effect against the other
If they have instructed the same lawyers
If they belong to the same parent company
If they distribute the same products
loesung: The first answer is correct. Two legal entities are exceptionally one party if their interests are so identical that a judgment against one would have **res judicata** effect against the other (Meril/Edwards).
einheit:u02a-5b.abschnitt: Art. 33(2) and 33(4) UPCA: the same parties

einheit:u02a-5c.frage: Does M-Srl become the defendants' straw man because it coordinates its defence with them?
loesung: **No!** The straw man doctrine can fulfil the criterion. However, a **common defence strategy** does not in itself make the second company the straw man of the first (CD Paris, Seoul Viosys/Emporia).
einheit:u02a-5c.abwandlung: M-Srl and the defendants closely coordinate their defence against E.
einheit:u02a-5c.abschnitt: Art. 33(2) and 33(4) UPCA: the same parties

einheit:u02a-5d.frage: May the central division decide on M-Srl's revocation action?
loesung: **Yes!** The bar in Art. 33(4) UPCA does not apply. The local division can take the parallel revocation action into account in its decision under Art. 33(3) UPCA and R. 118.2 RoP.
einheit:u02a-5d.merke: The same parties means the same legal entities; the exception requires an extension of res judicata.
einheit:u02a-5d.abschnitt: Art. 33(2) and 33(4) UPCA: the same parties

einheit:u02a-5e.titel: Art. 33(2) UPCA: the division first seised
einheit:u02a-5e.frage: Is the division first seised competent for a second infringement action by E against M-Ltd.?
loesung: **Yes!** If an infringement action between the same parties on the same patent is pending, the **division first seised** is competent for further infringement actions (Art. 33(2) UPCA).
einheit:u02a-5e.abwandlung: E wants to sue M-Ltd. before another local division for further deliveries.
einheit:u02a-5e.abschnitt: Art. 33(2) and 33(4) UPCA: the same parties

gruppe:u02a-6.sachverhalt: Before the Düsseldorf Local Division, the defendant files a counterclaim for revocation. After the written procedure, the division decides, without hearing the parties, to hear both actions itself. It does not request a technical judge because the technology is said to be simple.

einheit:u02a-6a.frage: Must the division hear the parties before choosing one of the options under Art. 33(3) UPCA?
loesung: **Yes!** The division decides on the three options **after hearing the parties** and at its discretion (R. 37.1 RoP; right to be heard under R. 264 RoP). The parties were not heard here.

einheit:u02a-6b.frage: Can the division dispense with the technical judge when hearing both actions together?
loesung: **No!** If the division chooses option (a), it hears both actions itself **and** requests the President of the Court of First Instance to allocate a **technically qualified judge** (R. 37.3 RoP). There is no discretion to dispense with this.
einheit:u02a-6b.merke: Option (a): hear both actions together, but only with a technical judge.

einheit:u02a-6c.frage: May the division refer the counterclaim to the central division and continue the infringement action itself?
loesung: **Yes!** That is option (b), **bifurcation**: the counterclaim is referred, and the infringement proceedings are stayed or continued. A stay should be ordered where there is a high likelihood that the patent will be revoked (R. 37.4 RoP). In practice, the divisions almost always choose option (a).

einheit:u02a-6d.frage: Can the division refer the entire case to the central division against the will of one party?
loesung: **No!** Option (c), referral of the entire case to the central division, requires the **agreement of the parties** (Art. 33(3)(c) UPCA).

einheit:u02a-6e.frage: May the defendant make its counterclaim conditional on a finding of infringement?
loesung: **Yes!** The infringement action and the counterclaim remain **separate actions**; the counterclaim may be made conditional on a finding of infringement (Emboline/AorticLab).

gruppe:u02a-7.sachverhalt: P-GmbH develops inhalation devices and plans to launch a new model in two years. It brings a revocation action before the central division against a patent of K-NV. K-NV has never sent it a warning letter; P-GmbH has not filed an opposition at the EPO.

einheit:u02a-7a.frage: Does the stand-alone revocation action belong before the central division?
loesung: **Yes!** Revocation actions belong to the central division (Art. 32(1)(d), Art. 33(4) UPCA). Which section – Paris, Munich or Milan – is decided by the IPC class (Annex II UPCA, R. 17.3 RoP).
einheit:u02a-7a.abschnitt: Art. 33(4) and 33(8) UPCA: revocation action before the central division

einheit:u02a-7b.frage: Is P-GmbH “concerned” by the patent, even though it does not yet market a product?
loesung: **Yes!** Standing to bring the action lies with any person **concerned** by the patent (Art. 47(6) UPCA). A person is concerned if it wants to clarify its **freedom to operate**, i.e. anyone who is or could become active in the technical field of the patent (CD Milan, Pari/Philips).
einheit:u02a-7b.merke: A person is concerned if it works, or wants to work, in the field.
einheit:u02a-7b.abschnitt: Art. 33(4) and 33(8) UPCA: revocation action before the central division

einheit:u02a-7c.frage: Does the action require a warning letter from K-NV?
loesung: **No!** Neither a warning letter nor a product on the market is required; Art. 47(6) UPCA only requires that the claimant is concerned (Pari/Philips).
einheit:u02a-7c.abschnitt: Art. 33(4) and 33(8) UPCA: revocation action before the central division

einheit:u02a-7d.frage: Must P-GmbH first file an opposition at the EPO?
loesung: **No!** A prior opposition at the EPO is not a prerequisite for a revocation action (Art. 33(8) UPCA).
einheit:u02a-7d.abschnitt: Art. 33(4) and 33(8) UPCA: revocation action before the central division

einheit:u02a-7e.frage: Can the UPC stay the revocation action?
loesung: **Yes!** If opposition proceedings are running in parallel, the Court may stay its proceedings where a **rapid decision of the EPO** may be expected (Art. 33(10) UPCA, R. 295(a) RoP).
einheit:u02a-7e.abwandlung: A third party has filed an opposition at the EPO; the decision of the opposition division is expected within a few months.
einheit:u02a-7e.abschnitt: Art. 33(4) and 33(8) UPCA: revocation action before the central division

kapitel:u02b.titel: R. 19 to 21 RoP: the Preliminary objection

einheit:u02b-0.titel: Preliminary objection: one month, three grounds
einheit:u02b-0.text: The defendant must contest jurisdiction **within one month** of service of the Statement of claim by lodging a **Preliminary objection** (R. 19.1 RoP). The grounds are exhaustive: (a) jurisdiction of the Court, including an opt-out, (b) competence of the chosen division, (c) language of the Statement of claim; a breach of Art. 47 CFR as such is not among them (Roku/Dolby). Before a regional division, the defendant may also request referral to the central division if the infringement has occurred in the territories of three or more regional divisions (R. 19.4 RoP, Art. 33(2) UPCA). If no Preliminary objection is lodged, the jurisdiction of the Court and the competence of the division are deemed **accepted** (R. 19.7 RoP) – the objection is then also lost on appeal (Sinocare/Abbott). The time limit for the Statement of defence continues to run (R. 19.6 RoP). The claimant may itself cure defects in the choice of division or language within 14 days; if it indicates a competent division, the judge-rapporteur **refers** the case (R. 19.5 RoP). The **judge-rapporteur** decides on the Preliminary objection after hearing the parties (R. 20.1 RoP) or deals with it in the main proceedings (R. 20.2 RoP) – the panel may do so too if the question has been referred to it under R. 102.1 RoP (Vivo/Sun Patent). If the judge-rapporteur allows the Preliminary objection, an appeal lies under R. 220.1(a) RoP; if he rejects it, only with leave under R. 220.2 RoP (R. 21.1 RoP). A **stay** under R. 21.2 RoP requires that an appeal has already been lodged (Sun Patent/Vivo).

gruppe:u02b-1.titel: What can the Preliminary objection raise?
gruppe:u02b-1.sachverhalt: B-AG is sued before a local division. Its lawyer gathers the objections and checks which of them belong in the Preliminary objection under R. 19 RoP.

einheit:u02b-1a.frage: Can B-AG argue in the Preliminary objection that an opt-out is registered for the patent?
loesung: **Yes!** R. 19.1(a) RoP expressly mentions the jurisdiction of the Court, including the objection that an **opt-out** under R. 5 RoP applies. Apart from that, there is only the competence of the division (R. 19.1(b) RoP) and the language of the Statement of claim (R. 19.1(c) RoP).
einheit:u02b-1a.abschnitt: R. 19 RoP: grounds and time limit

einheit:u02b-1b.frage: Can B-AG argue in the Preliminary objection that the patent is obviously invalid?
loesung: **No!** The list in R. 19.1 RoP is **exhaustive** (Roku/Dolby). B-AG challenges validity with a **counterclaim** in the Statement of defence (R. 25 RoP).
einheit:u02b-1b.abschnitt: R. 19 RoP: grounds and time limit

einheit:u02b-1c.frage: Does the objection that the claimant, as a non-exclusive licensee, lacks standing belong in the Preliminary objection?
loesung: **No!** Standing (Art. 47(3) UPCA) and all other objections belong in the **Statement of defence** (R. 23, 24 RoP). Formal defects of the Statement of claim are examined by the Registry (R. 16 RoP).
einheit:u02b-1c.abschnitt: R. 19 RoP: grounds and time limit

einheit:u02b-1d.frage: Does the time limit for the Statement of defence continue to run despite the Preliminary objection?
loesung: **Yes!** The time limit for the defence continues to run (R. 19.6 RoP). The Preliminary objection must be drafted in the language of the Statement of claim (R. 19.3 RoP).
einheit:u02b-1d.merke: The Preliminary objection only asks: this court, this division, this language? Everything else belongs in the Statement of defence.
einheit:u02b-1d.abschnitt: R. 19 RoP: grounds and time limit

einheit:u02b-1e.frage: Can B-AG make up for it by raising the division's lack of competence in the Statement of defence?
loesung: **No!** If no Preliminary objection is lodged, the jurisdiction of the Court and the competence of the division are deemed **accepted** (R. 19.7 RoP).
einheit:u02b-1e.abwandlung: B-AG lets the one-month time limit under R. 19.1 RoP expire.
einheit:u02b-1e.abschnitt: R. 19 RoP: grounds and time limit

gruppe:u02b-2.sachverhalt: V-Corp. lodges a Preliminary objection to jurisdiction before a local division. The judge-rapporteur refers the question to the panel under R. 102.1 RoP. The panel orders that the Preliminary objection be dealt with only in the main proceedings.

einheit:u02b-2a.frage: Must a Preliminary objection always be decided in advance?
loesung: **No!** The judge-rapporteur either decides on the Preliminary objection (R. 20.1 RoP) or informs the parties that it will be dealt with **in the main proceedings** (R. 20.2 RoP).
einheit:u02b-2a.abschnitt: R. 20 RoP: decision or main proceedings

einheit:u02b-2b.frage: Was the judge-rapporteur entitled to refer the question to the panel?
loesung: **Yes!** The judge-rapporteur may refer **any matter** to the panel (R. 102.1 RoP). Whatever the judge-rapporteur may do, the panel may also do after the referral (Vivo/Sun Patent).
einheit:u02b-2b.abschnitt: R. 20 RoP: decision or main proceedings

einheit:u02b-2c.frage: Does R. 102 RoP also apply in the written procedure?
loesung: **Yes!** R. 102 RoP is located in the section on the interim procedure, but applies **mutatis mutandis in the written procedure**. There too, the judge-rapporteur is in charge of case management (R. 18, R. 331.1 RoP), including the order in which issues are decided (R. 334(e) RoP) (Vivo/Sun Patent).
einheit:u02b-2c.abschnitt: R. 20 RoP: decision or main proceedings

einheit:u02b-2d.frage: Is the order to deal with the Preliminary objection in the main proceedings a rejection of the Preliminary objection?
loesung: **No!** It is not a rejection under R. 21.1 RoP, but a **case management** order. Where, as here, it comes from the panel, it can only be challenged with leave under R. 220.2 RoP or by way of discretionary review.
einheit:u02b-2d.merke: The judge-rapporteur manages the written procedure, but may refer any matter to the panel.
einheit:u02b-2d.abschnitt: R. 20 RoP: decision or main proceedings

gruppe:u02b-4.titel: The judge-rapporteur as judge in his own cause
gruppe:u02b-4.sachverhalt: Huawei sues Netgear before the Munich Local Division. Netgear lodges a Preliminary objection. The judge-rapporteur informs the parties that the Preliminary objection will be dealt with in the main proceedings (R. 20.2 RoP). Netgear applies for review by the panel; the judge-rapporteur himself rejects this application as inadmissible.

einheit:u02b-4a.frage: Can Netgear appeal directly against the communication under R. 20.2 RoP?
loesung: **No!** Unless otherwise provided, case management decisions of the judge-rapporteur or the presiding judge **cannot be appealed directly**. The remedy is an application for review by the **panel** (R. 333.1 RoP) (Netgear/Huawei).

einheit:u02b-4b.frage: Is the communication that the Preliminary objection will be dealt with in the main proceedings a case management decision?
loesung: **Yes!** The decision under R. 20.2 RoP is a case management decision; the panel must review it upon application under R. 333.1 RoP (Netgear/Huawei).

einheit:u02b-4c.frage: Must the panel decide on the admissibility of the application for review?
loesung: **Yes!** The **panel** decides on the admissibility of the application under R. 333.1 RoP (Netgear/Huawei; R. 333.4 RoP). The application must be lodged within 15 days (R. 333.2 RoP).
einheit:u02b-4c.merke: A review of the judge-rapporteur's decision is never decided by the judge-rapporteur himself.

einheit:u02b-4d.frage: Must Netgear apply for review by the panel before appealing?
loesung: **No!** If the judge-rapporteur rejects the Preliminary objection, he may, by way of exception to the general rule, grant leave to appeal. Netgear then has the **choice**: appeal or application under R. 333.1 RoP (Netgear/Huawei).
einheit:u02b-4d.abwandlung: The judge-rapporteur rejects the Preliminary objection and grants leave to appeal.

einheit:u02b-4e.frage: Can Netgear then immediately apply to the Court of Appeal for discretionary review?
loesung: **No!** Without leave, Netgear must first apply for review by the panel. An appeal lies against the panel's decision if the panel grants leave (R. 220.2 RoP), otherwise discretionary review (R. 220.3 RoP) (Netgear/Huawei).
einheit:u02b-4e.abwandlung: The judge-rapporteur rejects the Preliminary objection and does not grant leave to appeal.

gruppe:u02b-3.sachverhalt: The judge-rapporteur rejects V-Corp.'s Preliminary objection. V-Corp. applies for leave to appeal under R. 220.2 RoP and, at the same time, for a stay of the proceedings under R. 21.2 RoP. It has not yet lodged an appeal.

einheit:u02b-3a.frage: Does a stay under R. 21.2 RoP require that an appeal has been lodged?
loesung: **Yes!** R. 21.2 RoP allows a stay “if an appeal is lodged”. The appeal against the decision on the Preliminary objection must therefore **already have been lodged** (Sun Patent/Vivo).

einheit:u02b-3b.titel: Application for leave is not enough
einheit:u02b-3b.frage: Is the application for leave to appeal sufficient?
loesung: **No!** A mere application for leave under R. 220.2 RoP is not an appeal that has been lodged (Sun Patent/Vivo).

einheit:u02b-3c.frage: Can V-Corp. instead base the stay on R. 295(m) RoP?
loesung: **No!** As **leges speciales**, the special rules in R. 19 to 21 RoP take precedence over the general rules on stays in R. 295 ff. RoP (Sun Patent/Vivo).

einheit:u02b-3d.frage: Who in principle decides on the stay of first-instance proceedings under R. 295 RoP?
optionen: The President of the Court of First Instance
loesung: The first answer is correct. R. 295 RoP applies in both instances, but a stay of first-instance proceedings is in principle decided by the **Court of First Instance**, which knows the circumstances better and has discretion in case management (Sun Patent/Vivo).

einheit:u02b-3e.titel: The time limit continues to run
einheit:u02b-3e.frage: May V-Corp. wait with the Statement of defence until leave has been decided?
loesung: **No!** The Preliminary objection does not suspend the time limit for the Statement of defence (R. 19.6, R. 23 RoP). V-Corp. must file its defence in time.
einheit:u02b-3e.merke: R. 21.2 RoP requires an appeal that has already been lodged, and the time limit for the defence continues to run.
